summary: 1. Sep 26 posts the fiscal cycle's sharpest ore miss and its heaviest single crusher stoppage. 2. Total production landed at 20,832 BCM against a 21,767.2 BCM target (-4.30%), with ore falling 84.34% short of its 1,979.6 BCM target — the biggest ore miss this cycle after Sep 25's beat. 2. 3. A single 9h05m day-shift crusher maintenance stop (7:55 AM-4:10 PM) drove the lowest daily crusher feed reading this cycle (2,160 BCM), pulling MTD crusher stockpile throughput to just 3.79% of the 124,000 LCM monthly plan through day 2 of 30. 3. 4. The excavator fleet posted its sharpest single-day availability drop this cycle (63.99% daily, down from 66.37%), with EX-253 and EX-123 both extending their standing multi-day stoppages to eleven and five days respectively, while a follow-up maintenance email confirms DT-128's engine swap is nearly complete (release targeted end of day 27-Sep) and finally diagnoses DT-107's fault as coolant leaking onto pistons on cylinders 1 and 9. 5. See [[daily-production-report]] and [[fleet-availability-utilization]]. 6. The 27-Sep HOD meeting calls Sep 26 production RED against a stepped-up ~71,000 t target (actual 56,296 t, within 50 t of the workbook's own 56,246.4 t total) — the fourth different target figure this KB has seen cited across the last four HOD meetings (61-62k, then 70-75k, then a specific 71,000 t), still unreconciled with the workbook's own 58,771.44 t Sep 26 target. 7. The meeting says the October plan has not yet been formally received. 8. EX-123's swing control valve repair attempt (DRA-assisted) failed. 9. The team is investigating alternative options while the original 7-10 day replacement-parts ETA still stands; PC2000 parts remain a separate concern with an ETA around 6 October. WL-101 and WL-329 both open new faults the day after their prior faults cleared — WL-101's Engine Warning fault (77.08% avail) comes one day after its roughly 236-day Accident Damage record closed; WL-329's three concurrent jobs (SOS hydraulic/radiator action, 250-hour service, tyre change-out, 68.75% avail) follow directly after its Fuel Tank Cracked fault cleared inside a day. DT-344 opens a new Tire Puncher #04 breakdown (12h, 50.00% avail), adding to the tire-availability pressure the HOD meeting separately flags as a critical constraint (seven urgent tires, eleven sitting with the repair supplier roughly six weeks past a normal turnaround). No new daily INX-SUM survey workbook landed this pass — the newest file remains `260926-INX-SUM.xlsx`, already registered and compiled as Sep 25 data. [[survey-volume-reconciliation]] is unchanged this pass; Sep 26's own survey reading is due on a future pass. Source: `Production report/Oct 26/October Client Meeting Report-.xlsx` (Sep 26 data); `Maintanance Shedules/Oct 26/DailyAvailability_Final_Report (26-09-2025 ).pdf`; `HOD Meetings/HOD Morning Meeting 27 Sep 26.msg`; `Maintanance Shedules/Oct 26/RE EX-253 - DT128 breakdowns .msg`. `October Block Info.xlsx`, `October A & U.xlsx`, `DPR-October-2026.xlsx`, `October Daily Drill Meters Report-.xlsx`, `Daily Drill Sampling Record-2026.xlsx`, `DPR and A&U- October-2026.docx`, `Equipment running hours report -.xlsx`, `Grade Control Sheet October 2026.xlsx`, and `DIESEL CONSUPTION REPORTS Sep-2026.xlsx` registered, cross-check only. `Weekly Operational Review 26-Sept-2026.pptx` registered at index level only — its own Production Summary table still reads mid-September figures, a stale template carry-over. `Workshop Daily Task 27-Sep-2026.pdf` (both Sep 26 and Oct 26 copies) registered at index level, the standing pattern. Tasks: none created this pass. The unreconciled HOD-meeting target line and EX-123's failed repair attempt are logged as open questions in the affected articles rather than dispatched as action items. Important References, Notes & References, and Task Feedback Log workflows were not run this pass, per the task's own instructions. No content removed or renamed from RAW. ---
